butir.teks: Explanation of the reality of the intellect and its divisions

Know that people differ about the definition of the intellect and its reality, and most of them overlooked that this name is applied to different meanings, and that became the cause of their disagreement.

The truth that lifts the veil on this is that the word 'aql (intellect) is a name applied homonymously to four meanings, just as the name 'ayn, for example, is applied to several meanings, and the like of this. So one should not seek a single definition for all its divisions; rather each division is treated separately by uncovering it. The first is the attribute by which a human being is distinguished from all the other beasts, and it is that by which he is made ready to receive the theoretical sciences and to manage the subtle, reflective crafts. It is what al-Harith ibn Asad al-Muhasibi meant when he said, in defining the intellect, that it is an innate disposition by which the perception of the theoretical sciences is made ready, and it is as it were a light cast into the heart by which it is prepared to perceive things. He was not fair who denied this and reduced the intellect to mere necessary knowledge, for one who is heedless of the sciences and one who is asleep are both called intelligent on account of the presence of this innate disposition in them, despite the absence of the sciences. Just as life is an innate disposition by which the body is made ready for voluntary movements and sensory perceptions, so too the intellect is an innate disposition by which some animals are made ready for the theoretical sciences. And if it were permissible to equate the human and the donkey in the innate disposition and the sensory perceptions

and it were said, "There is no difference between them except that Allah Most High, by the operation of custom, creates knowledge in the human and does not create it in the donkey and the beasts," then it would be permissible to equate the donkey and an inanimate thing in life, and it would be said, "There is no difference except that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, creates particular movements in the donkey by the operation of custom."

For if the donkey were supposed to be a dead inanimate thing, it would be necessary to say that every movement observed in it, Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is able to create in it in the observed order.

Just as it is necessary to say that its distinction from the inanimate thing in movements was only through an innate disposition particular to it, which is expressed as life, so likewise the human's distinction from the beast in perceiving the theoretical sciences is through an innate disposition that is expressed as the intellect. It is like the mirror, which differs from other bodies in reflecting images and colours by an attribute particular to it, namely polish.

Likewise the eye differs from the forehead in attributes and forms by which it is made ready for sight. So the relation of this innate disposition to the sciences is like the relation of the eye to sight, and the relation of the Qur'an and the revealed Law to this innate disposition, in leading it to the unveiling of the sciences to it, is like the relation of the light of the sun to eyesight. This, then, is how this innate disposition should be understood.

The second is the sciences that come into existence in the person of the discerning child, namely the possibility of the possible and the impossibility of the impossible, such as the knowledge that two is more than one and that a single person cannot be in two places at one time. This is what some of the theologians (mutakallimun) meant when they said, in defining the intellect, that it is some of the necessary sciences, such as the knowledge of the possibility of the possible and the impossibility of the impossible. This too is correct in itself, because these sciences exist and calling them intellect is evident. What is invalid is only that one denies that innate disposition and says that nothing exists but these sciences.

The third is sciences gained from experiences through the course of events, for one whom experiences have seasoned and whose ways have refined is said to be intelligent in the customary sense, and of one who lacks this attribute it is said
that he is dull, inexperienced, ignorant. This, then, is another kind of knowledge called intellect.

The fourth is that the strength of that innate disposition reaches the point that a person knows the consequences of matters and subdues the appetite that calls to immediate pleasure and overpowers it. When this strength is attained, its possessor is called intelligent in that his advancing and holding back follow what reflection on consequences requires, not the rule of immediate appetite. This too is among the distinguishing properties of the human by which he is distinguished from all other animals. The first is the foundation, the root, and the source
and the second is the branch nearest to it.
And the third is a branch of the first and the second, since by the strength of the innate disposition and the necessary sciences the sciences of experience are gained.
And the fourth is the final fruit and the furthest end. The first two are by nature and the last two by acquisition.
Therefore 'Ali (may Allah honour his face) said
I saw the intellect to be two intellects ... the innate and the heard.
The heard is of no benefit ... if there is no innate.
Just as the sun is of no benefit ... when the light of the eye is barred.

The first is what is meant by his saying (peace and blessings be upon him), "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has not created a creation more honoured with Him than the intellect" (١), and the last is what is meant by his saying (peace and blessings be upon him), "When people draw near through the doors of righteousness and good deeds, draw near yourself through your intellect" (٢). It is also what is meant by the saying of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) to Abu ad-Darda' (may Allah be pleased with him), "Increase in intellect and you will increase in nearness to your Lord." He said, "May my father and mother be your ransom, and how can I do that?" He said, "Avoid what Allah Most High has forbidden and perform what Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has made obligatory, and you will be intelligent. And do righteous deeds, and you will increase in the immediate life of this world in elevation and honour, and you will attain through them, in the Hereafter to come, nearness to your Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, and might" (٣). And on the authority of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, that 'Umar, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, and Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with them) entered upon the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) and said, "O Messenger of Allah, who is the most knowledgeable of people?" He said, "The intelligent one." They said, "Then who is the most devout of people?" He said, "The intelligent one." They said, "Then who is the most excellent of people?" He said, "The intelligent one." They said, "Is the intelligent one not he whose manliness is complete, whose eloquence is evident, whose hand is generous, and whose standing is great?" So he said, ⟦QS 43:35⟧ "The intelligent one is the God-conscious (muttaqi), even if he is lowly and abased in this world" (٤). He said in another hadith, "The intelligent one is only he who believes in Allah, believes His messengers, and acts in obedience to Him" (٥). It seems that the original meaning of the name in the original language is for that innate disposition, and likewise in usage, and it was applied to the sciences only in that they are its fruit, as a thing is known by its fruit, so it is said, "Knowledge is fear, and the knower is the one who fears Allah Most High."
For fear is the fruit of knowledge, so the word would be like a figurative use for something other than that innate disposition. But the aim is not to investigate language.

The point is that these four divisions exist and the name is applied to all of them, and there is no disagreement about the existence of any of them except the first division, but the correct view is that it exists; rather, it is the origin.

These sciences are as if they were contained in that innate disposition by nature, but they appear in existence when a cause occurs that brings them out into existence, so that it is as if these sciences were not something coming upon it from outside, and as if they had been latent in it and then appeared. An example is water in the earth: it appears by digging a well and gathers and becomes distinct to the senses, not by something new being driven to it. Likewise the oil in almonds and the rose water in roses. Therefore Allah Most High said ⟦QS 7:172⟧

What is meant by it is the acknowledgement of their selves, not the acknowledgement of the tongues, for they divided in the acknowledgement of the tongues, wherever tongues and persons were found, into one who acknowledges and one who denies. Therefore Allah Most High said ⟦QS 43:87⟧ Its meaning is that if their states are considered, their selves and their inner beings bear witness to that ⟦QS 30:30⟧ that is, every human being is created by nature with belief in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, indeed with knowledge of things as they are; I mean that they are as if contained in it because of the nearness of its readiness to perceive.

Then, since belief is implanted in the selves by nature, people divided into two groups: those who turned away and forgot, and they are the disbelievers, and those who set their thought moving and remembered, so he was like one who bore testimony, forgot it through heedlessness, and then remembered it.
Therefore Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said ⟦QS 5:7⟧ And calling this type remembrance is not far-fetched, so remembrance would be, as it were, of two kinds, one of them
that he remembers an image that had been present in existence in his heart but became absent after the other existence.
And the other is that he remembers an image that was contained in him by nature.
These are realities evident to one who looks with the light of insight, but heavy upon one who takes comfort (١) in hearsay and imitation rather than unveiling and direct seeing.

Therefore you see him floundering over such verses and being arbitrary, and in interpreting remembrance as the acknowledgement of the selves he resorts to all kinds of arbitrary readings, and kinds of contradictions in the reports and verses appear to his imagination, and perhaps that overcomes him until he looks at them with an eye of contempt and believes there is incoherence in them.

His likeness is that of the blind man who enters a house and stumbles in it over the vessels arranged in the house, and says, "What is wrong with these vessels, that they are not lifted from the path and returned to their places?" So it is said to him, "They are in their places; the fault is only in your sight."

So likewise the defect of insight takes the same course, and is graver and greater than it, since the self is like the rider and the body like the horse, and the blindness of the rider is more harmful than the blindness of the horse. Because the inner insight resembles the outer sight, Allah Most High said ⟦QS 53:11⟧ and Allah Most High said ⟦QS 6:75⟧ the verse, and He named its opposite blindness, so Allah Most High said ⟦QS 22:46⟧ and Allah Most High said ⟦QS 17:72⟧ And these matters that were unveiled to the prophets, some were by sight and some were by insight, and all were called seeing.
In sum, whoever's inner insight is not piercing, nothing of religion clings to him except its husks and its illustrations, without its kernel and its realities.
These, then, are the divisions to which the name "intellect" applies.
